body:
Greg's direction, relayed by Engram::Advisor (TermAl mailbox b9d13887 #2878 and Engram Advisor #2459, 2026-10-31 15:49Z), verbatim: „DL560 ma 72 cory i 256 GB pamieci; jego zdaniem nie wymaga synchronizacji dostepu i powinien obslugiwac rownolegle zadania. Prosze usunac sztuczny jeden slot na DL560 i zaplanowac rownolegle niezalezne gate i cargo, z osobnymi worktree/targetami i rozsądnymi limitami faktycznych zasobow; potwierdzic praktyczne wykorzystanie."

SHARED DL560 RULE (rev 2, 15:51Z): proposed by Engram::Fable (ebe242f7 #5664), concurred by Termal::Fable2 with one addition. It supersedes my interim rev 1 (max 3, disk ≥ 100 GB, load < 100) and the dl560-runner-checklist r17 line "2 concurrent jobs, 1 Engram + 1 TermAl".
- No per-project slot and no fixed job count.
- Each job runs in its own fresh detached worktree, with its own target and a throwaway HOME and TMPDIR, in each project's own runner clone. Only the toolchain and the cargo registry cache are shared.
- Admission at launch: MemAvailable ≥ 64 GiB, free disk ≥ 60 GB plus the job's expected footprint (40 GB until measured), and 1-minute load < 64. Otherwise the job is queued with the reason.
- Fable2's addition: if any other job is running at launch, the new job's environment gets CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=48. It can be dropped if measurement shows it's unnecessary.
- Heavy and stress jobs record the concurrent load. Each START lists the concurrent job ids.
- A contention failure is diagnosed as a failed gate and never retried until green.
- Each project's coordinator schedules its own lanes with a named GO per job. There is no cross-project GO.
- After the first parallel window, the Runner reports peak concurrency, RAM, load and per-job wall time.
Central Windows stays one Cargo job at a time; this covers DL560 only.
